Chapter 9: Finishing as a Repeatable Habit
Let’s dive into something that really makes a difference—not just starting, but actually finishing. See, finishing isn’t a one-time thing. It’s a habit, something you can build up and make part of who you are. Each time you wrap up a project, no matter how small, you’re stacking up confidence. You start to create this positive feedback loop, where completion feels good and encourages you to do it again. Over time, finishing just becomes part of your identity. It’s a trait you can count on, especially when your motivation dips.
So, how do you make finishing a real habit? Well, it helps to create routines and simple rituals that nudge you toward completion. Here are a few ideas:
First, try setting up daily or weekly review sessions. Carve out a few minutes to check in on your progress and tweak your plans. This regular touchpoint keeps you honest and on track.
Next, think about pre-commitment. Decide ahead of time when and how you’ll tackle your work. That way, you don’t have to rely on willpower in the heat of the moment.
Closure rituals can also make a big difference. Celebrate wrapping up a project, even in a small way. Maybe it’s a quick reflection, or treating yourself to your favorite coffee. These little moments help reinforce just how great finishing feels.
And here’s a simple trick—try stacking your finishing habits onto routines you already have. For example, after your morning coffee, review your checklist for the day. Linking new behaviors to existing habits makes them much easier to stick with.
Picture this: Someone ends each workday by scanning their to-do list and planning out tomorrow. Just that simple ritual brings a sense of closure, and gets their mind ready for the next set of tasks.
When you treat finishing like a skill you can practice, you take the pressure off and make success more likely. It’s not just about getting one thing done—it’s about making completion second nature. And the more you finish, the more natural it feels, and the less likely you are to slip back into old habits of leaving things unfinished.
So, if you want to see real progress, make finishing part of your daily rhythm. Over time, you’ll find it becomes effortless—and that’s when the magic really starts to happen.
